name: DNCn_QN
expansion: Debiased NonClosure under the null, Quantile-Normalized
tagline: The queen: an in-house ABCD closure term that only pushes where the counts can see, now in three forms

caveat.text: Internal, exploratory studies. Nothing on this page is an ATLAS result; results are given in words, and the numbers stay in the internal record.

intro.problem: An ABCD background estimate holds only if the two network scores are independent on background. Decorrelation penalties shrink dependence everywhere [@disco2020][@kasieczka2021], including where the counts cannot resolve it, and a term that drives non-closure to zero can be met by fitting statistical noise or by emptying the signal region.
intro.value: Penalizing non-closure in units of its own counting noise targets the quantity the estimate relies on, closure in the regions used [@cms2025tec], and stops pushing once the residual is within noise. The classifiers stay free wherever closure already holds, so separation is spent only where it buys closure.
intro.approach: Each training step draws [[cut-pair|cut pairs]] at background quantiles inside the [[trained-band]], forms [[soft-count|soft region counts]] and their propagated variance, and penalizes closure only above one unit of counting noise. Three forms differ in what they count and how they pool: [[qb]], [[qdr]] and the pooled [[tau-hat-squared|$\hat\tau^2$]].
intro.goals: Sealed, hash-pinned closure terms with their own unit tests, run as the β axis of the BASELINE sweep in both regions; a pre-registered record of where each form should work; and a clear account of which dependence the queen removes and which she only relocates.

questions: Does a hinged, noise-scaled closure term reach held-out closure that matches or beats decorrelation alone, at a smaller cost in separation?
Does it remove dependence between the two scores, or move it into the high-score corner beyond the cuts it trains on?
Does treating non-closure as a random variable with a measured null give closure that holds more steadily across cuts and sample sizes than one hinge per cut?

components.name: The per-cut statistic
components.subtitle: Shared by every form
components.summary: Enforce ABCD closure directly, but only where the data can resolve [[closure|non-closure]], so the networks are never pushed to fit statistical noise. Every form builds the same per-cut quantity before pooling it.

items.label: Cuts
items.detail: Each step draws [[cut-pair|cut pairs]] at [[background-quantile|background quantiles]] on both scores, inside the [[trained-band]]; the boundaries are [[held-fixed|held fixed]] for the gradient and never learned

items.label: Soft counts
items.detail: Each background event joins regions $A$ to $D$ through a sigmoid of its distance to each cut: $N_X = \sum_i w_i\, m_X(i)$, with $m_X(i)$ between 0 and 1. These are [[soft-count|soft counts]]; grading uses [[hard-count|hard counts]]

items.label: Residual
items.detail: $g_k = N_A - N_B N_C / N_D$: how far region $A$ misses its [[abcd-prediction]]

items.label: Noise floor
items.detail: $\tilde F_k$, the [[noise-floor|variance of $g_k$]] propagated from the four soft counts, held fixed for the gradient

items.label: Statistic
items.detail: [[z-squared|$z_k^2 = g_k^2 / \tilde F_k$]], the residual in units of its own noise; $z_k^2 \approx 1$ is counting noise alone

items.label: Hinge
items.detail: The [[hinge]] $\max(0,\, z_k^2 - 1)$: zero while the residual is within noise, rising only above it

components.name: QB: the hinge on the training batch
components.subtitle: Sealed in BASELINE as the β term
components.summary: The original queen: the per-cut hinge averaged over a few cut pairs drawn on each training batch, with soft counts on [[count-space|probabilities]]. It is taken byte for byte from the hash-sealed code genealogy.

items.label: Loss
items.detail: $L_{\mathrm{QB}} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} \max(0,\, z_k^2 - 1)$ over the cut pairs of one training batch

items.label: Checks
items.detail: Matches the reference implementation in loss and gradient on real background scores; when decorrelation already holds every drawn cut within noise, the hinge gives exactly zero gradient

items.label: Where it fits
items.detail: The working point is locked, and the aim is less bias without stretching the score shapes

items.label: Limit
items.detail: It lowers the bias but does not even out closure from one cut to the next

components.name: QDR: the hinge on a background draw
components.subtitle: Same hinge, new inputs
components.summary: The same per-cut hinge as QB, fed a separate [[background-draw]] every step instead of the training batch, with more cut pairs and soft counts on [[count-space|logits]]. The draw gives every cut pair usable counts in all four regions.

items.label: Loss
items.detail: $L_{\mathrm{QDR}} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} \max(0,\, z_k^2 - 1)$ over the cut pairs of one background draw

items.label: Name
items.detail: Q for the queen, D for the draw she is fed

items.label: Where it fits
items.detail: The working point is not locked: cuts are scanned, several signal regions are used, or the analysis region sits in the tail

items.label: Cost
items.detail: It stretches NN2's background logits and gives up a little separation

components.name: τ̂²: non-closure as a random variable
components.subtitle: Proposed successor · pooled excess over a measured null
components.summary: A point target for closure can be met in unphysical ways: cuts that empty the signal region, or closure tighter than the counts can resolve. [[tau-hat-squared|$\hat\tau^2$]] treats the fractional non-closure at each cut as a draw with counting noise plus a real spread, the quantity an analysis carries as its closure systematic, and penalizes only the spread across many cuts that exceeds counting noise.

items.label: Statistic
items.detail: The same per-cut $z_k^2$, summed over the cut pairs: [[q-statistic|$Q = \sum_k z_k^2$]]

items.label: Null
items.detail: [[shuffle-null|$Q_{\mathrm{null}}$]], measured each step by permuting NN2's scores among background events; this keeps both score distributions and the cut positions and removes only the dependence

items.label: Loss
items.detail: $\hat\tau^2 = \max(0,\, Q - Q_{\mathrm{null}}) / W$: one hinge on the pooled excess, with [[w-normaliser|$W = \sum_k \tilde P_k^2 / \tilde F_k$]] making it a fraction

items.label: Scale
items.detail: Because the excess is a fraction, the term does not grow with the number of events it sees, and its weight needs no rescaling between batch, draw or region sizes

items.label: Inputs
items.detail: The same background draw, logit counts and cut pairs as QDR, so the two differ only in how they pool

items.label: Status
items.detail: Confirmed on fresh seeds beside QDR; on closure the two are not yet told apart

components.name: One family of closure terms
components.subtitle: How the in-house terms relate
components.summary: At a single cut with an analytic null, $\hat\tau^2$ reduces to the per-cut hinge times the fractional noise floor; without the hinge and pooling it becomes the unhinged tail term [[dnc-flr]]. All of them are read as one model of closure, so each sweep result says something about the others.

items.label: Unchanged
items.detail: Cuts are drawn from background quantiles and never learned, a closure term never [[epoch-selection|chooses its own training epoch]], and grading is on held-out cuts with a shuffle null

items.label: Run with
items.detail: Every form goes on top of [[disco|DisCo]], never instead of it: $L = \mathrm{BCE}_1 + \mathrm{BCE}_2 + \alpha\,\mathrm{dCor}^2 + \beta\,L_Q$, with $L_Q$ the form in use and α, β the [[loss-weights]]

items.label: Graded by
items.detail: The BASELINE grader and its dependence spectrum, so a closure gain can be read as removal or as relocation

results.title: Every form helps on top of DisCo
results.text: In both regions, adding any form of the queen to [[disco|DisCo]] moves the distribution of [[pull|pulls]] over random cut pairs toward the noise-only reference. Raising DisCo's own weight does not do the same.

results.title: Only the draw-fed forms even closure out across cuts
results.text: In the endcap, QDR and $\hat\tau^2$ narrow the spread of closure from cut to cut; QB moves the average but keeps DisCo's spread. In the [[barrel-endcap|barrel]] the spread is already close to counting noise, so the gain there is in the offset.

results.title: The trade
results.text: QB leaves the score shapes alone. QDR and $\hat\tau^2$ stretch NN2's background logits and cost a little separation.

results.title: Shared limit
results.text: Every form shrinks the closure error but none changes its direction: region $A$ stays above its ABCD prediction in every run.

links.title: Where she is benchmarked
links.text: The queen is the β axis of the BASELINE sweep: alone, paired with DisCo, and with the tail term, in both regions, under the same gate, grader and lock rule as every other loss family.

links.title: Architecture search
links.text: TRUSS rebuilds the closure-term models, so architecture choices are judged with the queen in the loss rather than only with plain cross-entropy.

open.text: QDR and $\hat\tau^2$ are not yet told apart on closure: which one should hold the β slot?
No form changes the direction of the closure error, only its size.
She works only on a background mix like the one she was trained on; she does not survive an [[htmiss|$H_T^{\mathrm{miss}}$]] shift.
The hinge forms need their β set per region, because $z_k^2$ grows with the events counted; the same β is several times weaker in the barrel. $\hat\tau^2$ is built not to need this.
